subject: GCP marketplace SKU duplication + GST entity split — action items

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Unexpected GCP invoice line + GST split between AU entities

Hi Jordan / Marissa,

We received the October marketplace invoice (attached) and it looks like two distinct SKU lines were billed twice under different internal project IDs. One of the lines includes a GST component that was attributed to our AU parent entity; the other was attributed to a newly created Australian subsidiary. We open the marketplace invoice PDF and the usage CSV and it's unclear which usage records map to which legal entity.

Can Redwood confirm whether the marketplace metering emitted duplicate usage_ids for the same consumption window, or if this is a problem on our listing side? We need to know whether GCP should reissue a single corrected invoice or if Gridware should submit an internal apportionment so we can claim GST correctly.

Attached: 2026-10-invoice-Gridware-GCP-12345.pdf, usage_report-2026-10-gridware.csv

Thanks,
Adrian Torres
Finance Manager — Gridware Technologies
adrian.torres@gridware.co

1) Can you confirm the Gridware seller account IDs for both entities (parent vs subsidiary)? The usage CSV has project labels but I want the legal-entity tax IDs so we can correlate to the seller-side mapping in our listing.

2) I'm looping in Karthik (Marketplace Ops) and Marissa (Finance liaison) — we'll pull the Redwood-side metering logs for the October window and compare the emitted usage_ids. If marketplace-billing@gcp-partnerops has any insight on duplicate metering events in October, that would be helpful.

Subject: Re: Unexpected GCP invoice line + GST split between AU entities

Team / Adrian — I've pulled the metering logs for 2026-10 across the Gridware listing. Preliminary findings:

- There are two distinct SKU IDs (sku_0x7a and sku_0x7b) that show near-identical hourly emission patterns for 2026-10-12 00:00:00 -> 2026-10-12 05:00:00. The usage_ids tied to those lines are different, but the payloads look like duplicates (same timestamps, same token counts).
- On our side, that indicates the Redwood submission to GCP included two listing entries for closely-related feature gates that both emitted metering for the same customer usage in the October window. It's likely a listing configuration issue rather than marketplace-side double-billing.

Implications: if GCP invoices both SKUs as separate lines, GST will be calculated per line and may be attributed to different seller tax IDs depending on the listing mapping. We should:

A) Provide Gridware a dedupe manifest (usage_id pairs + timestamps) so they can cross-check with their finance team.
B) Recommend Gridware request a single corrected invoice from GCP (credit one line and reissue consolidated) OR accept internal reallocation and request a GST credit memo.

I'll attach the dedupe manifest in a follow-up.

—Karthik
Marketplace Operations Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: dedupe_manifest-Gridware-2026-10.csv (will follow)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Adrian Torres <adrian.torres@gridware.co>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected GCP invoice line + GST split between AU entities

Adrian, Jordan — quick note from Finance: to process a GST reclaim or internal apportionment we need the following from Gridware:

- Confirmed legal entity names, ABNs (Australian Business Numbers) for both billed entities.
- A signed statement describing which invoice line(s) correspond to which legal entity for October.
- If you want Redwood to pursue a marketplace credit, sign-off that Redwood invoices (or credits) Gridware for the consolidated amount — GCP will need a marketplace partner request from us.

If Gridware prefers we request GCP reissue a single consolidated invoice, we need authority to open a partner dispute ticket on your behalf (we will include the dedupe manifest). Otherwise Gridware can accept Redwood's internal apportionment and we will provide a GST allocation worksheet for your tax filing.

Timeline: if we get entity ABNs and sign-off today, we can open a partner dispute with GCP by EOD tomorrow and ask for a credit + corrected invoice within 10 business days. If Gridware opts for internal apportionment, we will deliver the allocation worksheet within 3 business days.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: none
